questions.help: 1 Influence of the vehicle in traffic collisions 1.2 Vehicle safety featuresToday many vehicles incorporate safety features as a standard matter of course. These provide the driver, occupants and other road users with a high level of safety and security when travelling. However, statistics show that new vehicles with greater technological advances, suffer proportionately more accidents than older vehicles, when it would have been logical for the reverse to apply; namely, older vehicles to suffer more collisions.One of the reasons might be that very few drivers know how the new technology works and what the systems provide for their vehicles so that such features, rather than being advantageous, become an inconvenience and sometimes a danger.(Página 61 del manual 'Learning to drive')1 Influence of the vehicle in traffic collisions 1.2 Vehicle safety featuresWhilst, on the other hand, there are many drivers who, knowing that their vehicles have these latest developments installed, feel more secure and, consciously or unconsciously, take more risks, unaware and oblivious to the fact that any security system always operates within certain limits.For a safety system to be effective the driver must know how to operate it and how it works and, above all, how to drive accordingly. It is therefore very important to read carefully the technical manual of the car and learn how to properly use the safety systems installed.(Página 61 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES                 3 Brakes 3.7 Emergency braking  Vehicles with ABSIn an emergency situation a driver of a vehicle fitted with ABS should step firmly on to the brake pedal and keep constant pressure applied. questions.help: ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES               3 Brakes3.7 Emergency braking Vehicles without ABSIf an unplanned emergency occurs to an automobile braking without ABS, the driver should apply maximum force on the brake without locking the wheels. If the wheels lock the braking distance is increased and directional control is lost. The vehicle stability could also become affected. Normally, if you lock the rear wheels and the car skids, it can result in the car spinning; if the front wheels lock the car will continue in a straight line, with a loss of directional control.Therefore, the brakes should be applied firmer and stronger than normal, until just before the wheels lock. The principle is to apply more pressure than normal but the pressure must be reduced before the wheels lock and then reapplied until the vehicle stops or the need to take evasive action has passed.(Página 66 del manual 'Learning to drive')ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES                 3 Brakes 3.7 Emergency braking  Vehicles with ABSIn an emergency situation a driver of a vehicle fitted with ABS should step firmly on to the brake pedal and keep constant pressure applied. questions.help: ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES     4 Wheels4.2 TyresThe tread of the tyre is the part that is in contact with the road surface. The adhesion depends largely on the type and condition of the tyre, (composition, tread pattern, wear, etc.) the weight of the vehicle transmitted through to the tyres and the composition and state of the road surface. Favourable adherence is provided by road surfaces, which are in good condition made either of tarmarcadum, asphalt or concrete. Whilst adhesion is reduced on roads that are in bad condition, or made out of cobblestones, or are wet, covered in snow, ice, leaves, oil, etc.Faults associated with the tyres are the main cause of road traffic collisions attributable to the vehicle, they account for more casualties than all other vehicle systems put together.(Página 68 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES             4 Wheels    4.2 Tyres  4.2.3 The tread patternThe tread pattern is the set of grooves in the tread of a tire. In addition to gripping the road surface, it must guarantee good drainage away of the surface water from the tyre. The adhesion between the tyre and the road is reduced when the tyre is worn.All tyres, (including retreads) must always comply with the legal requirements. This includes, not only the tyre tread and depth of pattern but also other abnormalities relating to the tyre-wall and tread, inflation pressure, bulges, exposed cords, cuts and other signs of irregular wear, and also the mixing of tyres etc. Basically the carcass (housing) must comply with all legal requirements.The tyres of the vehicles within categories M1, N1, O1 and O2 (See Unit 1, article 14) must, when used on the public roads (or places recognised as public thorough fares), have a minimum depth of tread, of 1.6 mm, in a continuous band in the main grooves of the contact surface.Note: There are other requirements relating to the depth of tread and pattern.(Página 70 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES             4 Wheels    4.2 Tyres  4.2.3 The tread patternThe tread pattern is the set of grooves in the tread of a tire. In addition to gripping the road surface, it must guarantee good drainage away of the surface water from the tyre. The adhesion between the tyre and the road is reduced when the tyre is worn.All tyres, (including retreads) must always comply with the legal requirements. This includes, not only the tyre tread and depth of pattern but also other abnormalities relating to the tyre-wall and tread, inflation pressure, bulges, exposed cords, cuts and other signs of irregular wear, and also the mixing of tyres etc. Basically the carcass (housing) must comply with all legal requirements.The tyres of the vehicles within categories M1, N1, O1 and O2 (See Unit 1, article 14) must, when used on the public roads (or places recognised as public thorough fares), have a minimum depth of tread, of 1.6 mm, in a continuous band in the main grooves of the contact surface.Note: There are other requirements relating to the depth of tread and pattern.(Página 70 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES             4 Wheels    4.2 Tyres  4.2.3 The tread patternThe main grooves are defined as, the wide grooves located in the central zone of the tread band that covers the central three-quarters of the tread width.There is no obligation for a motorcycle to have a minimum depth of tyre tread; but the recommendation is that, it should be at least 1.6 millimetres.(Página 70 del manual 'Learning to drive')
